newsitem.title: HAITI: Four killed, many injured during Haitian Carnival.
newsitem.headline: Four killed, many injured during Haitian Carnival.

text.p: Four people were killed and about 300 hurt in three days of annual Carnival celebrations in Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince this week, radio reports and hospital officials said on Wednesday.
A woman was killed when a badly built float collapsed, Radio Ginen said. Three other people were stabbed to death in the crowds, according to hospital officials.
Most of the injuries were from fights or the pressure of the packed crowds.
"There was a lot of the usual shoving and fistfights but I felt safer this year," said Carnival-goer Valerie Delerme, who took her two children to watch the parade.
Last year, different security agencies clashed in the crowds. On the final day one person was killed when a panicked police officer fired his gun into a menacing crowd.
This year, the foreign-trained Haitian National Police, formed 18 months ago, suspended all other arms permits and carried out weapons checks throughout the three days.

Police Chief Pierre Denize marched with an entourage of heavily armed agents through the crowd in a show of force on the first night. Police carried billyclubs and submachineguns to keep order amongst the estimated 500,000 Haitians in the streets.
President Rene Preval, wearing a baseball cap backwards, danced and ran through crowds on Tuesday night, with his security detail trailing behind him.
